text_blocks.snippet: Common cardiac medications include ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, diuretics, statins, antiplatelets, and anticoagulants. These medications are prescribed to manage conditions like high blood pressure, heart failure, high cholesterol, and to prevent blood clots.
snippet_highlighted_words: ACE inhibitors, beta-blockers, diuretics, statins, antiplatelets, and anticoagulants

list.title: ACE Inhibitors:
list.snippet: These medications, such as lisinopril and ramipril, help relax blood vessels, lower blood pressure, and reduce the heart's workload.

list.title: Beta-Blockers:
list.snippet: Examples include atenolol and metoprolol. They slow the heart rate and reduce the force of heart contractions, often used for heart failure, angina, and arrhythmias.

list.title: Diuretics:
list.snippet: Also known as "water pills," these medications, like furosemide and hydrochlorothiazide, help remove excess fluid and sodium from the body, lowering blood pressure.

list.title: Statins:
list.snippet: Medications like atorvastatin and simvastatin help lower cholesterol levels, reducing the risk of heart disease and stroke.

list.title: Antiplatelets:
list.snippet: Aspirin and clopidogrel are examples. They prevent blood platelets from sticking together, reducing the risk of blood clots.

list.title: Anticoagulants:
list.snippet: Warfarin, heparin, and newer oral anticoagulants like rivaroxaban prevent blood clots by affecting clotting factors.

list.title: Calcium Channel Blockers:
list.snippet: These medications, like amlodipine and diltiazem, relax and widen blood vessels, lowering blood pressure and relieving chest pain.

list.title: Nitrates:
list.snippet: Nitroglycerin is a common example. They dilate blood vessels, increasing blood flow to the heart and relieving chest pain (angina).

list.title: Antiarrhythmics:
list.snippet: These medications, like flecainide, help regulate heart rhythm in patients with arrhythmias.
